description: {"time": 1783112237654, "blocks": [{"id": "eo6ki3pwpb", "data": {"text": "Sugar \u2014 a Rongao Sacco matatu \u2014 wore its name with sweet irony on Nairobi's commuter routes. The design likely played on double meanings: the sugary treats that fuelled passengers in traffic, or the sugar-daddy jokes that pepper matatu banter. Dennis Muraguri's woodcut captures the lettering's confident swagger and the subtle details that made this matatu a local favourite. The piece belongs to Muraguri's ongoing documentation of Nairobi's mobile culture, where matatus function not just as transport but as community billboards reflecting inside jokes, social commentary, and shared humour. The woodcut technique \u2014 with its bold lines and high contrast \u2014 suits the punchy, graphic nature of matatu lettering. This print adds a pop of graphic wit to any wall.
